title: Hosted API — developer-first voice & billing playbook
content:
Executive summary:

This doc is a working playbook for short-form and conversational messaging aimed at engineers evaluating hosted inference. Goal: test a lean set of developer-forward value propositions + 3 pricing-language variants that map to different buying triggers (experimentation, scale, enterprise).

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Many vendors lead with feature lists (token price, model catalog, region coverage) that read like a spec sheet; developers respond better to fast, concrete outcomes (time to working proof, predictable cost during growth, integration friction).
- We want the Hosted API to land as the tool that gets from prototype -> production with minimal infra/ops investment and predictable unit economics.

Target audiences (prioritized):
1) Product/feature engineers at AI-native startups who want fast iteration (first 30 days).
2) Platform/ML infra engineers at scale-ups who need predictable latency and cost (30–90 days).
3) Early enterprise buyers evaluating security and SLAs (pilot -> POC).

Core developer-first positioning (short lines for hero/banner):
- "Code, don't configure: deploy LLM features in hours, not quarters."
- "Predictable token economics, built for apps that scale."
- "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — move to production without rewiring."

Message pillars (explainer bullets for site/email/landing):
- Fast to integrate: SDKs, drop-in examples (chat, summarize, embeddings), and a one-click starter that returns a usable response in under 90 seconds.
- Production-ready by design: transparent latency profiles, route-level SLOs, and integrated fallback policies for graceful degradation.
- Cost controls that matter: per-request sampling, auto-batching recommendations, and a cost simulator showing per-route USD/Tk across 1k–1M monthly requests.
- Safety & data controls: ephemeral logs option, customer KMS support, and VPC-ready private deployments for regulated data.

Quickstart angles (experiments to test):
A) "Hello world" in 5 lines — GitHub gist + runnable code sandbox that returns a chat completion and an example of streaming tokens. CTA: create API key and run.
B) Template gallery — curated 3 templates (support summarizer, search ranking reranker, personalized email generator) with copy/paste prompts and expected latencies & token costs. CTA: fork template to project.
C) Cost-first demo — UI that lets devs toggle batch size / quantization and shows simulated monthly bill delta. CTA: sign up to preserve configuration.

Pricing-language drafts (three tones):
1) Experiment-first (friendly, low-commit):
"Try Hosted API free — generous credits and transparent per-token billing. Pay only for what you use; upgrade to committed capacity when you need consistent throughput."
- Emphasize: free credits, per-token pricing, no upfront, easy upgrade path.

2) Scale-first (ops-oriented):
"Predictable throughput, predictable spend. Reserved capacity plans give you guaranteed GPU throughput and volume discounts — plus tools to model unit economics before you commit."
- Emphasize: volume tiers, reserved capacity, cost simulator & batching suggestions.

3) Enterprise (compliance-focused):
"Private deployment options and enterprise SLAs for production-critical features. Custom billing and consolidated invoices for multi-team orgs."
- Emphasize: invoicing, contracts, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations.

Pricing copy experiments (short snippets to A/B):
- Variant X: "$0.00 — get started. Usage billed per token after credits. Exact per-token price depends on model; see model catalog for details."
- Variant Y: "From $X/Tk — Developer tier; volume discounts at commits over $10k/mo. Reserved instances for predictable latency."
- Variant Z: "Transparent unit economics: simulate request patterns and get an instant monthly estimate before committing."

Competitive landscape notes (quick scout):
- OpenAI: strong brand + broad dev adoption; friction often arises around unit economics at scale and private deployments.
- Anthropic: safety-forward positioning, competitive in high-safety use cases.
- Cloud providers (AWS/Azure/GCP): deep infra integration, but heavier integration and higher ops surface for inference; less startup-friendly onboarding.
- Inference runtimes/self-hosted vendors: lower sticker cost at scale but higher ops burden.

Differentiation checklist (concrete proof points to build):
- One-click starter that wires to a project and runs a real query in <2 minutes (capture analytics on time-to-first-query).
- Cost-simulator widget that ties to the model catalog and shows token-level math for routes.
- Benchmarks: per-model latency percentiles and a "when to pick X model" cheat sheet that maps to expected token cost.
- Example success stories: 2–3 short case blurbs (dev-focused) showing time-to-ship and cost savings.

Tone guidance & microcopy rules:
- Keep copy short, action-oriented, and engineer-focused; avoid marketing fluff. Use exact numbers where possible.
- When describing price, always show an example call cost (e.g., "Greeting bot: 120 tokens ≈ $0.003") alongside per-token figures.
- Use "you" to speak directly to developers: "You can spin up a chat endpoint and test with real user prompts in minutes."

Questions / open decisions (for product & legal):
- How to handle model-level price variability in short copy without overwhelming devs? Proposed: link to model catalog with a single-line estimate for common patterns (short chat, long generation, embeddings).
- What free-credit size best balances signal vs noise? Proposal: $300 credits decaying over 90 days for new accounts. Needs finance sign-off.

Low-effort experiments to run in next 6 weeks:
- Landing page hero A/B: "Code, not configure" vs "Predictable token economics" (measure activation and credit redemptions).
- 5-line quickstart sandbox — instrument time from page load -> first successful API call.
- Pricing microcopy test on signup flow: show per-token example vs. omit; measure churn on first invoice.

Next steps & owners:
- Product: build cost-simulator prototype (Rajesh) — due in 4 wks.
- DevRel: create runnable 5-line sandbox & 3 template gallery entries (Nina) — PR by EOW.
- GTM: craft hero copy variants + meta-test plan (Tom) — coordinate with growth for 2-week landing experiments.

Appendix: short microcopy snippets (ready-to-use)
- "Start free with $300 in credits — experiment, build, and benchmark."
- "Drop-in SDKs for Node/Python. Examples for chat, embeddings, and reranking."
- "Reserve capacity when you need consistent latency — contact sales for custom SLAs."

Notes to reviewers: informal, rough — this is meant to seed landing content + in-product copy and to inform a small set of A/B tests. Prefer short, measurable experiments over wide redesigns.

End of doc.
